questions.q: ___ of my parents are teachers.

questions.explanation: 'Neither of' for 'not one nor the other' of two.
questions.q: ___ of the two films was interesting.

questions.explanation: 'None of' for zero out of three or more.
questions.q: ___ of the students passed — the exam was too hard.
___ my friends came to the party — it was great!

questions.explanation: 'Neither of' + singular verb: 'neither of them lives'.
questions.q: She has two brothers. ___ of them lives abroad.

questions.explanation: 'None of' for zero out of a group; 'you can take them' shows they're not mine.
questions.q: ___ of these three books are mine — you can take them.
Which sentence is correct?
___ of my sisters is married.

questions.explanation: 'All three books' — 'all' for the whole group.
questions.q: I've read ___ three books — they're all fantastic.

questions.explanation: 'None of' + singular verb for zero of an uncountable noun.
questions.q: ___ of the cake was left.
My parents are ___ retired.
There were only two of us, and ___ of us knew the answer.

questions.explanation: 'None of' for zero out of a larger group.
questions.q: The hotel had ten rooms, but ___ of them was clean.
___ my arms are tired after the workout.

questions.explanation: After 'none of', use an object pronoun: 'none of them', not 'none of they'.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?
She invited ___ her twenty classmates to the party.

questions.explanation: 'Neither of' for two things + singular verb.
questions.q: ___ of the two options is perfect.
We ate ___ the pizza.

options: None of the boy were there.
None of the boys were there.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
___ the money was spent.
